_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). This is the right-hand edge of the scroll in the summit band, and it OVERLAPS t006 heavily: t007 x = t006 x - 0.234 for the shared left three quarters, so the tree line, the great pale face and the bottom-edge tree crown are the same objects seen again, shifted left, plus a new right-hand strip that t006 does not contain. Content: the left half is one enormous pale summit face in long parallel 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre strokes with almost no wash; the right half is a steeply raking cliff whose strokes fan down to the lower left in long combed bands. Real foliage, all of it small distant trees with a visible vertical trunk under a flat dotted crown: (1) the crest tree line at upper left, climbing from x~0.11,y~0.29 to x~0.38,y~0.02 (the t006 upper-centre line); (2) the loose group of flat-crowned trees at x 0.39-0.58, y 0.30-0.47, the clearest foliage in the tile, with a pale blue wash behind it (the t006 right-ridge group); (3) a thin file of the same trees climbing the ridge to the upper right, x 0.55-0.83, y 0.02-0.40; (4) a NEW object not present in t006: a small grove on a ledge at the lower right, x 0.83-1.0, y 0.71-0.87, where warm ochre trunks are plainly visible under dark crowns with a trace of blue-green wash; (5) the blue-green crown of the big near tree clipped by the bottom edge at x 0.21-0.56. DECOYS, in order of how badly they will fool a colour or darkness threshold: (a) the raking right cliff, x 0.60-1.0 below y 0.30 -- its combed hemp-fibre bands read as sprays of pine needles at thumbnail size and there is no trunk and no crown anywhere in them; (b) the moss-dotted rock spine at the top right, x 0.84-1.0, y 0.02-0.28, a chain of 点苔 dabs on a crest that mimics the genuine tree file immediately to its left -- the separating test is that these dabs lie along the rock fold and have no vertical stroke beneath them; (c) the dark shadowed crest across the top centre, x 0.30-0.58, y 0.00-0.16, grey wash plus moss, no tree glyphs. One sub-floor real object is deliberately omitted: a bare fine-line sapling at about x 0.28-0.33, y 0.55-0.63 on the summit face, no leaf mass, must not move.

objects.name: group of flat-crowned trees on the ridge, centre
objects.note: the same group as summit-t006 ridge-trees-right-lower, shifted left by 0.234. Dark vertical trunk strokes under horizontally spreading dotted crowns, pale blue wash brushed behind them. Box contains bare silk between the crowns and ridge rock along its lower edge -- key on the dot clusters, not the box

objects.name: file of trees climbing the right ridge, lower half
objects.note: SEARCH REGION -- a narrow DIAGONAL line of small trees running lower-left to upper-right; most of the box is cliff. Continues ridge-trees-centre up the same ridge

objects.name: file of trees climbing the right ridge, upper half
objects.note: SEARCH REGION, same diagonal file continued to the top edge. Individually these trees are well under the size floor; they are worth registering only as a band, and any sway must be tiny or they will jitter. The moss-dot spine at x>0.84 is NOT part of this and must be excluded

objects.name: trees on the upper-left crest, lower half
objects.note: SEARCH REGION. Small dark tufts strung along a ridge silhouette that climbs to the right, so the lower-right half of the box is the rock body of that ridge. Same objects as summit-t006 crest-trees-centre-lower

objects.name: trees on the upper-left crest, upper half
objects.note: SEARCH REGION, the same crest line continued to the top edge where it is clipped. Its right end abuts the dark shadowed crest, which is rock

objects.name: small grove on a ledge, lower right
objects.note: NOT VISIBLE IN t006 -- this is the object that justifies cataloguing t007 separately. Three or four trees with unmistakable warm ochre trunks standing under dark tufted crowns, with a faint blue-green wash in the foliage; they sit on a small ledge in the middle of the raking cliff. The single most convincing foliage in the tile after ridge-trees-centre. Box includes the ledge rock below the trunks

objects.name: crown of a large tree clipped by the bottom edge
objects.note: the same tree as summit-t006 tree-crown-bottom-centre, shifted left by 0.234: rounded outlined leaf clusters washed pale blue-green, the only leaf colour of that kind in the tile. Only the head of a much larger foreground tree that lives below y 4136 in the master

objects.name: ochre trunk and bare branches of the bottom-edge tree
objects.note: warm ochre wood forking into bare upward twigs above the leaf mass. RIGID -- leaves pivot about it

objects.name: the great pale summit face, left half
objects.note: one vast rounded rock mass in long hemp-fibre strokes, filling the left half of the tile top to bottom. The largest single rigid region in the tile. NEVER animate

objects.name: raking cliff with combed hemp-fibre bands, right
objects.note: THE PRINCIPAL DECOY OF THIS TILE. Long parallel 牛毛皴 strokes combed diagonally down to the lower left, punctuated with 点苔 moss chains. The fanned strokes look like sprays of needles at thumbnail size; magnified there is no branch, no trunk, no repeated leaf glyph. grove-ledge-lower-right sits INSIDE this region and is the one part of it that is genuinely foliage -- cut that grove out, then treat everything remaining here as rigid stone

objects.name: moss-dotted rock spine, top right
objects.note: DECOY, and the nastiest one here because it sits directly beside ridge-trees-right-upper and looks the same at a distance. A chain of 点苔 dabs laid along the crest fold of a rock spine. Test: no vertical trunk stroke under any dab, and the chain bends with the rock contour instead of standing on a ledge

objects.name: dark shadowed crest across the top centre
objects.note: DECOY. Wet grey wash on the shaded side of a crest with moss dabs on top; the darkest passage in the upper tile and easily mistaken for a tree mass. Clipped by the top edge. Same object as summit-t006 rock-ridge-dark-top

objects.name: rock shelves in the lower centre
objects.note: pale stepped ledges under the summit face, running down to where the bottom-edge tree stands. Rigid
